_why: Scenarios for a REAL policy wording: HDFC ERGO's my: Optima Secure.
Fetch the PDF with evals/real/fetch_policies.py; it is never committed.
Written for M27, before any code for it and before any run of these cases, from the
policy's own wording. Same author as the system, so not fully independent.
What prompted them: the plan-comparison table near the end of the PDF has rows like
'1.6 Post-Hospitalization 180 days 180 days ...'. The pipeline types those rows (ids
1.5#2 and 1.6#2) as 60- and 180-day WAITING PERIODS. They are cover windows: how long
before admission and after discharge expenses are paid. Read as waiting periods they
would block every claim in the first six months. These cases check that they don't,
and that the real windows (1.5 and 1.6) still decide the questions they should.
Conventions: this policy has no compulsory co-payment, so a payable claim is
`covered` (the optional Aggregate Deductible is assumed not chosen). Ids with '#' are
repeats of a number, from citation_ids() in app/pipeline/scenario.py. The 30-day
initial waiting period is Excl03: M27 made the segmenter split Section C at its IRDAI
codes and use the code as the id. The cases were first written citing '1#4', the id
it had before that split; only the id was renamed, no expectation changed.
The last two cases were added during M27, after the segmenter began splitting
Section C into Excl01/02/03 and before any run of them: they check the split did not
lose the two bars it separated. Ids Excl01 and Excl02 are the IRDAI codes the
policy prints, which the segmenter now uses as these clauses' ids.

cases.scenario: I was admitted to hospital with typhoid 45 days after buying this policy. It is my first health insurance.
cases.why: The 30-day initial waiting period (Section C 1.c, in Excl03) is served at 45 days, and typhoid is not on the specified disease list. Nothing else applies.

cases.scenario: Four months after taking this policy I was hospitalised for five days with dengue. I had no insurance before.
cases.why: Four months serves the 30-day initial waiting period; dengue is neither pre-existing nor on the specified disease list.

cases.scenario: I was admitted to hospital with typhoid 20 days after buying this policy. It is my first health insurance.
cases.why: An illness within 30 days of the first policy is excluded (Section C 1.c, in Excl03), with no prior cover to waive it and no accident.

cases.scenario: I fractured my leg in a road accident ten days after buying this policy and was admitted to hospital for surgery.
cases.why: The 30-day initial waiting period exempts accidents, and nothing else applies to an accidental fracture.

cases.scenario: I had my appendix removed in hospital last month. I have held this policy for two years. Can I claim the medicines and follow-up visits for the three months after discharge?
cases.why: Post-hospitalisation expenses are paid for up to 180 days after discharge (1.6), and the stay itself is admissible: two years serves the 30-day wait and appendicitis is not on the list.

cases.scenario: I was discharged after a hospital stay for pneumonia seven months ago. I have held this policy for three years. Can I claim the physiotherapy I am having now?
cases.why: Post-hospitalisation expenses are paid only up to 180 days after discharge (1.6); seven months is past it.

cases.scenario: I had scans and blood tests 75 days before I was admitted for a planned surgery. I have held this policy for three years. Are those tests covered?
cases.why: Pre-hospitalisation expenses are paid only up to 60 days before admission (1.5); 75 days is outside it.

cases.scenario: I need surgery for a hernia that was found last month. I bought this policy 14 months ago and it is my first health insurance.
cases.why: Hernia is on the specified disease/procedure list, excluded until 24 months of continuous cover (Excl02). Fourteen months have not served it, there was no prior cover, and nothing suggests an accident.

cases.scenario: I have had diabetes for six years and declared it when I bought this policy a year ago. Now I am admitted to hospital because of complications of my diabetes.
cases.why: Diabetes predates the policy, so it is a pre-existing disease, excluded with its direct complications until 36 months of continuous cover (Excl01). One year has not served it.
